evidence: All six files (AddTaskToProjectUseCase, AssignTaskUseCase, CreateProjectUseCase, CreateUserUseCase, ListProjectTasksUseCase, MarkTaskDoneUseCase) declare `implements UseCase<..., ...>` with a single `execute` method.
src/application/use-cases/AddTaskToProjectUseCase.ts and src/application/use-cases/ListProjectTasksUseCase.ts both call the domain's `parseTaskStatus` instead of validating status themselves.

src/application/use-cases/AssignTaskUseCase.ts hands assignment to `task.assignTo(user)`, and src/application/use-cases/MarkTaskDoneUseCase.ts hands state changes to `task.markDone()`, so the transition rules stay in the entity.
src/application/use-cases/CreateProjectUseCase.ts and src/application/use-cases/CreateUserUseCase.ts use the IdGenerator port and the entity factories (`Project.create`, `User.create`).
Every use case returns its output through the shared DTO mappers `toTaskDto`, `toProjectDto` or `toUserDto`.
The NotFoundError lookup guard repeated in AddTaskToProjectUseCase, AssignTaskUseCase, ListProjectTasksUseCase and MarkTaskDoneUseCase is boilerplate, not a duplicated business rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All six files deal with one concern: application use-case orchestration for the project/task/user domain. They follow the same pattern throughout. Each one implements the UseCase<Input, Output> port, gets domain repositories and IdGenerator through constructor injection, delegates business rules to domain entities and value objects (Task.create, task.assignTo, task.markDone, Project.create, User.create, DueDate.fromIso, parseTaskStatus), and returns results through the shared DTO mappers (toTaskDto, toProjectDto, toUserDto). No use case skips a repository or the DTO mappers, and none re-implements a domain invariant. Status parsing lives in the domain's parseTaskStatus, and due-date validation lives in DueDate.fromIso. The repeated "findById, then throw NotFoundError if undefined" check is a small guard that every use case needs. It is not a duplicated business invariant, because the error type and the meaning of "not found" are defined once in the domain.
